solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chance acquaintance embraces this writer, a tonic

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: a pick-up is someone met by chance, often casually
the setter referring to himself

explanation.surface: Someone met by chance hugs the writer, which proves a real tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: PICK-ME-UP: the writer sits inside PICK-UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pick-me-up is anything, often a drink or medicine, that restores energy or spirits, as a tonic does.

clue.text: Wherein you might see pharaoh's head, height swathed in perfume?

definitions.text: Wherein you might see pharaoh's head

indicators.note: to be swathed in is to be wrapped inside cloth, so the pieces go within

parts.note: scent is a perfume

indicators.note: the head of a word is its top or first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the ruler's title
H is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: Where you'd spot an Egyptian king's head, perfumed and wrapped up like a mummy.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'pharaoh's head' do double duty: in the definition, the head a crown sits on; in the wordplay, the first letter. P comes first, and H goes inside SCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The pschent was the double crown of ancient Egypt, worn on the pharaoh's head, so his head is seen in it.

clue.text: Antidepressant I lug around outside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the pole goes round the other piece

parts.note: a lug is an old name for a pole or rod, the measure of length
rind is the outer layer or skin

explanation.surface: A patient hauling a bag of antidepressants around outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lug' looks like a verb, to carry; it is the obsolete measuring rod. 'Outside' is a noun here, the rind.
explanation.definitionFit: Iprindole is a tricyclic drug formerly prescribed to treat depression.

clue.text: Pet you can get from Tesco's

indicators.note: something you can get from a source is made out of it, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of the store's name with its possessive s

explanation.surface: A pet that can be bought at Tesco, a big British supermarket chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a noun, an animal; it is the verb, to pamper.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet someone is to indulge and fuss over them, which is what cosset means.

clue.text: *Sensational

parts.note: the asterisk marks the Azed competition word, for which solvers write their own clue
the setter supplies only a plain meaning: exaggerated for emotional effect

explanation.walkthrough: In an Azed competition puzzle one clue is replaced by a bare definition; readers send in clues for it, and this is that entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensational in its sense of lurid and overdramatised matches the stagey, exaggerated emotion of melodrama.

clue.text: Senior yeoman bringing up some longhorn oxen

indicators.note: in a down light, bringing up reads the letters from bottom to top
some means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A senior farmhand herding a few longhorn cattle up the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The yeoman is not a farmer but one of the Yeomen of the Guard, the royal bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: An exon is one of four officers commanding the Yeomen of the Guard, the British sovereign's bodyguard.

clue.text: Nanny he treated with a pill; protein constituent

indicators.note: something treated has been processed or worked on, so the letters change their order

parts.note: the letters of these words
the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A nanny gives a man a pill as treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenylalanine (here spelt without the final e) is an essential amino acid, one of the building blocks of protein.

clue.text: Left inside nearest to fire

indicators.note: inside places one letter within the word that follows it

parts.note: one's kin are one's nearest and dearest, close family
standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Something left inside, closest to the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Here kiln is a verb: to bake in a kiln. 'Nearest' gives KIN through the phrase nearest and dearest.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiln pottery is to bake it hard in an oven, which potters call firing it.

clue.text: Unit of weight with origins in Korea and the Indies

indicators.note: origins are starting points, so take the first letter of each word that follows

parts.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A unit of weight that originated in Korea and the East Indies.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is nearly true: the unit is East Asian in origin.
explanation.definitionFit: The kati, or catty, is a traditional weight of East and Southeast Asia, about 600 grams.

clue.text: I'm flagging around end of marathon, in one piece but antiquated

definitions.note: in one piece is ENTIRE; 'but antiquated' asks for its old spelling

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first phrase encloses the letter

parts.note: I am flagging, rendered as I and a verb for weakening

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A runner near the finish of a marathon, flagging but still intact.
explanation.walkthrough: The N goes after the I, inside I TIRE. 'But antiquated' marks the answer as an obsolete spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Intire is an old spelling of entire, meaning whole or unbroken.

clue.text: Striving exists in what represents Japan?

indicators.note: in places the first item within the second

parts.note: Japan is the land of the rising sun, and a sun rising in a down light reads upwards
is means exists

explanation.surface: Effort as a feature of the national symbol of Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: Japan's emblem is the rising sun, so SUN is written rising, upwards in this down light, with IS inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nisus is a literary word for effort or striving, a conscious impulse towards a goal.

clue.text: Special school for geeky swot

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for special
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A special school catering for nerdy, hard-working pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks educational but is the collective noun for whales, as pod is.
explanation.definitionFit: Spod is British slang for a dull, studious, socially awkward person, a nerd or swot.

clue.text: Type notes about Europe?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to spy is to note or observe
EC is the European Community

explanation.surface: Kinds of written remarks on Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like a noun but is a verb, observes.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or sort, as is a type.

clue.text: NZ-style picnic, no good in endless shower

indicators.note: in puts the first item inside the second
something endless has had its final part cut off

parts.note: a hail is a shower of ice pellets, or of anything
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A New Zealand picnic, spoilt by rain that never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: A hangi is a Maori earth oven; 'NZ-style' flags the regional word, and 'shower' is a weather shower, not a wash.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangi is a Maori earth oven and the outdoor feast cooked in it, a New Zealand kind of picnic.

clue.text: One in skiing venue botched test — in appropriate gear?

definitions.note: the clue's 'in' belongs with it: the answer is what one would be in

indicators.note: in places one item within the venue that follows
something botched is bungled, its letters messed up

parts.note: one as the indefinite article
skiers go down a slope
the four letters of the word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at the ski resort fails a test, though dressed the part.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'One' goes in after the first letter of the slope, and the bungled test follows. The question mark admits the definition is a hint about ski clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Salopettes are padded bib-and-brace trousers worn for skiing, exactly the gear suited to the slopes.

clue.text: Protein creating a fellow's bodily firmness

parts.note: belonging to a man
muscle tone is the body's firmness

explanation.surface: A protein supplement that gives a man a firm, toned physique.
explanation.definitionFit: Histones are a class of proteins around which DNA is wound in the cell nucleus.

clue.text: Prudent, skirting small island of crude rock

indicators.note: skirting means running round the edge of something, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: politic means shrewd or prudent
IS is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A cautious sailor steering clear of a rocky islet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' signals abbreviation: island shortened to IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisolitic describes rock made of pisolite, a coarse limestone of pea-sized grains, so of a rough rock.

clue.text: Plunge into lake, e.g. Windermere? — getting tangled with grim reed

indicators.note: tangled letters are knotted up and need straightening into a new order
the answer plus the other words make up the jumble, so those other words are taken away from it

parts.note: every letter of the phrase, abbreviation included
these letters are the part of the jumble that is not the answer

explanation.surface: Diving into Windermere and getting caught up in nasty reeds.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: the answer together with GRIM REED is an anagram of E.G. WINDERMERE, so take those eight letters away and four are left.
explanation.definitionFit: Enew is an old falconry and literary word meaning to drive or plunge into water, as into a lake.

clue.text: Endless hell? Girl coming around to give young parents a break

indicators.note: coming around means encircling, so the girl wraps round the other piece

parts.note: bit is slang for a girl or young woman

indicators.note: something endless has its final letter removed

parts.note: the abyss is the bottomless pit of hell

explanation.surface: A girl dropping round to give exhausted new parents a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' as a girl is dated British slang; 'Endless hell?' looks like a cry of despair from the tired parents.
explanation.definitionFit: To babysit is to look after a child while its parents go out, giving them time off.

clue.text: Fancy! Prisoners fed with such bivalves

definitions.note: the answer is a genus name, so it names a kind of these creatures

indicators.note: something fed with another holds it inside, so the letters lie within the preceding words

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that convicts are served shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cypris is a genus of tiny freshwater ostracods, crustaceans enclosed in a two-valved shell.

clue.text: Possibly impenetrable lock securing one wrongfully

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the lock grips the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress
one as the indefinite article
ill as an adverb, badly or wrongly

explanation.surface: A lock that may be unpickable, wrongly fastened on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Land with no tracks or paths through it may well be impossible to get through, hence the question-mark qualifier.

clue.text: Muscle put into excursion in a way that should attract punters?

definitions.text: in a way that should attract punters?

indicators.note: put into places one item inside another

parts.note: a sally is a short trip or outing
ab is short for an abdominal muscle

explanation.surface: Adding muscle to a sales trip to win over customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punters' here are customers, a British informal word.
explanation.definitionFit: Done salably means done in a way that makes something easy to sell, so appealing to customers.

clue.text: Less than half tobacco crumbled with e.g. naan — it flavours snuff

indicators.note: crumbled things break into bits that can be put together differently
fewer than half the letters of a seven-letter word means only its opening three

parts.note: the first three of its seven letters
every letter of the phrase, abbreviation included

explanation.surface: Bits of tobacco broken up with Indian flatbread, used to flavour snuff.
explanation.definitionFit: The tonka (or tonga) bean is a fragrant seed with a vanilla-like scent, traditionally used to perfume snuff and tobacco.

clue.text: What's ground for Abos? Not one will include made-up road

indicators.note: made-up means invented, a fresh construction of the letters
to include is to hold inside, so the first piece wraps the other

parts.note: no means not one
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about Aboriginal land and a road that has been invented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abos' is a dated and now offensive term for Aboriginal Australians. 'Ground' is the past participle of grind, not land.
explanation.definitionFit: Nardoo is an Australian clover-like fern whose spore cases were pounded into flour by Aboriginal people.

clue.text: Baronet holds urn up, revealing votes cast

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the word is written from bottom to top
holds means contains, so the first piece goes round the other

parts.note: Bt is the abbreviation for baronet
an olla is an earthenware pot or urn

explanation.surface: A baronet lifts the ballot urn to show how people voted.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot is the collection of votes cast in an election, as well as the process.

clue.text: Openings of a minute measure in human body yielding sweat?

definitions.note: a phrase describing a state, standing for the adjective

indicators.note: in places the selected letters within the body

parts.note: clay is a poetic word for the mortal human body

indicators.note: openings are the beginnings, so take the first letter of each following word

parts.note: the starts of the two nouns minute and measure

explanation.surface: Tiny measurements taken on a person's body as it sweats.
explanation.walkthrough: Only minute and measure contribute letters; 'a' is part of the surface. Clay for the body is a literary and biblical usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Clammy describes skin that is damp and sticky, as when it is breaking into a cold sweat.

clue.text: Bar (of a kind) that converts club into pub

parts.note: the two letters club has that pub lacks
turning one thing into another means using it as the other
the letter pub has where club has those two

explanation.surface: A kind of bar that turns a club into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is an instruction: replace CL in club by P and you get pub, i.e. CL AS P. 'Bar' looks like a drinks counter, matching club and pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A clasp is a bar attached to a medal ribbon naming the action or campaign served in.

clue.text: How Texans address others in reverse of liberal song (apostrophe)

indicators.note: in reverse means read backwards, from the end to the start

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
a lay is a short narrative poem or song

explanation.surface: Texan speech patterns explained through a backwards liberal ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: L and LAY together give LLAY, read backwards. The bracketed note warns of the apostrophe in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Y'all, a contraction of you all, is the Southern US second-person plural greeting used in Texas.

clue.text: Barley producing great gallons

parts.note: big means great in size
g is an abbreviation for gallons

explanation.surface: Barley crops yielding vast quantities of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigg is a Scots and northern word for a hardy four-rowed barley.

clue.text: A glacis fashionable in limestone

indicators.note: fashionable read as able to be fashioned, so these letters can be shaped anew

parts.note: the seven letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A sloping fortification bank built in stylish stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashionable' looks like praise; it is read as 'can be fashioned', reshaping the letters. A glacis is a slope in front of a fort.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaglia is a fine-grained Italian limestone, usually reddish, of the Upper Cretaceous.

clue.text: I'm husky — hate initially having to leave singers

indicators.note: having to leave means a letter departs from the word that follows

parts.note: a choir is a body of singers

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word beside it

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A hoarse singer hating having to quit the choir.
explanation.walkthrough: Husky here is not hoarse but made of husk; the answer speaks as itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Coir is the fibre taken from coconut husks, so it can describe itself as of the husk.

clue.text: A divine, I translatred Latin including nothing extra

indicators.note: including takes the zero into the group of letters to be worked

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: translated text is rendered into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a clergyman or divine
taken as written
the word's own letters
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A clergyman confesses to translating Latin with nothing added.
explanation.walkthrough: The source prints 'translatred', a typo for translated. 'Divine' is a noun, a clergyman, abbreviated by his degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional means added on or further, the same as extra.

clue.text: Shake second of dice in board game

parts.note: shog is an old and dialect word meaning to shake or jog

indicators.note: second of points to the letter in position two of the following word

parts.note: its second letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to rattle the dice during a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Shogi is Japanese chess, a strategy game played on a nine-by-nine board.

clue.text: Gathering in essence led by bishop

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
an essential oil is the essence of a plant; 'in' is part of the phrase, as oil is in essence

explanation.surface: A meeting at its core, presided over by a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering' suggests an assembly, but it is a gathering of pus. 'Led by bishop' puts B first.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering is an old word for an abscess or swelling full of pus, which is what a boil is.

clue.text: TV feature presenting antithesis of Con Government?

parts.note: pros and cons are opposites
G is an abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A television programme presenting the opposite of Conservative rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con Government' reads as a Conservative government; Con is split off as the opposite of pro.
explanation.definitionFit: Prog is informal short for programme, a feature broadcast on television.

clue.text: Rank of former cavalry officer and others in old-fashioned clothing

indicators.note: clothing wraps round a body, so the outer word goes round the inner one

parts.note: corny means trite and dated
etc, et cetera, means and others

explanation.surface: An old cavalry officer's rank, alongside others, in outdated uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' looks like a noun for uniform but is a verb, dressing one word in another. A cornet was the lowest commissioned officer in a cavalry troop.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornetcy is the commission or rank of a cornet, a cavalry officer who once carried the troop's standard.
